f64_normal_note: Float64 normals use the 1024-layer ziggurat of SPEC.md Appendix A in every port, and every row with f64_normal true is measured with it. A new Float64 normal row must carry ziggurat true.

ports.name: C
ports.note: The mt19937 figures move with code layout: in a program with only that loop, std::mt19937_64 with std::uniform_real_distribution<double> reaches 8.2 GiB/s.

ports.name: CUDA
ports.note: Each row first runs its own fill for two seconds, then times 21 fills, and the table gives the median. In the last run the fastest lay at most 4 % above the median on every row. cuRAND has no 8-, 16- or 64-bit integer output for Philox, so curandGenerate writes the same bytes as 32-bit words, and it has no half floats, bools, bounded integers or exponentials. Those rows compare with the nearest call.

ports.name: JAX
ports.note: cuRAND has no exponentials and no bounded or 64-bit integer output, so those rows give the nearest call: the uniform the exponential reads, or curandGenerate into the same bytes.

ports.name: PyTorch
ports.note: cuRAND has no 8-, 16- or 64-bit integer output for Philox, no bounded integers and no exponentials, so the cuRAND column gives the nearest call for those rows: curandGenerate into the same bytes, or the uniform the exponential reads.

ports.name: WebGPU
ports.note: No WebGPU library ships a generator, so the GPU baseline is a plain Philox4x32-10 shader with the same mul_hi as the Tandem shader. The derived rows compare with its raw words, marked *.

ports.name: Kokkos
ports.note: cuRAND has no 64- or 8-bit integer output for Philox, no bounded integers and no exponentials, so those rows give the nearest call: curandGenerate into the same bytes, or the uniform the exponential reads.

ports.name: Java
ports.note: cuRAND has no 64-bit integer output for Philox, no bounded integers and no exponentials, so those rows give the nearest call: curandGenerate into the same bytes, or the uniform the exponential reads.

ports.name: SYCL
ports.note: Each row first runs its own fill for two seconds, then times 21 fills, and the table gives the median. After the two seconds every fill runs at the card's 250 W power cap, so the rows give the capped rate. Where cuRAND has no such output the column gives the nearest call: it has no 8-, 16- or 64-bit integers for Philox, so curandGenerate writes the same bytes as 32-bit words, and no half floats, bools, bounded integers or exponentials.

ports.name: Metal
ports.note: MPS has uint32 words, float32 uniforms and float32 normals. The rows it has no draw for compare with its uint32 words of the same byte count, or its float32 uniforms for the exponentials, marked *.

ports.name: MLX
ports.note: MPS has no bounded integers and no exponentials, so those rows compare with its uint32 words or float32 uniforms, marked *.
